title: Best Water Purifier Under Rs 25,000 in India (2026): 4 RO+UV Picks Ranked
description: We ranked 5 RO+UV water purifiers under Rs 25,000 by TDS handling, filter cost and tank size -- four stand out, and one popular model to skip.
short_desc: Four RO+UV picks worth buying -- and one to skip.

headings.text: What actually matters in a water purifier under Rs 25,000

cta.headline: Want the full spreadsheet?
cta.sub: Compare 25+ RO+UV purifiers side-by-side -- TDS handling, tank size, filter cost, real user complaints.

faq.q: Is a Rs 20,000 water purifier really better than a Rs 10,000 one?
faq.a: Yes, in three measurable ways: TDS adjustment (mineralizer adds back calcium and magnesium that RO strips out), filter life (premium filters last 12 months vs 6 on budget models), and tank build quality (food-grade steel vs plastic on cheap units). The cheap ones work, but taste flatter and filter replacements add up faster.

faq.q: Do I need UV if I have RO?
faq.a: For municipal tap water in Indian metros, RO alone is sufficient. UV adds protection against bacteria and viruses in case the RO membrane is aging or feed water is contaminated. For borewell water or tanker-supplied water, both RO and UV are essential.

faq.q: How much do water purifier filters cost annually?
faq.a: Budget purifiers cost Rs 1,500-2,500 per year in filters. Premium purifiers like the picks below average Rs 1,800-2,200 per year -- similar total cost but with better membrane life. The Aquaguard and Pureit service networks include filter cost in annual maintenance contracts (AMC) for Rs 2,500-4,000 per year.

faq.q: What TDS level is safe to drink after RO?
faq.a: RO strips TDS down to 30-50 ppm, which is too low for taste and health (the WHO recommends 100-300 ppm). Premium purifiers add a mineralizer stage to bring TDS back to 150-200 ppm. If you drink RO water straight, add a pinch of pink salt or use a mineralizer cartridge.

faq.q: Can a water purifier work without electricity?
faq.a: No. RO+UV purifiers need power to run the pump and UV lamp. The picks below all have built-in tanks so you can still drink during power cuts (6-12 hours of storage). For areas with frequent long outages, consider a non-electric gravity-based purifier as a backup.

tldr_pick: The Eureka Forbes Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+MTDS is the best water purifier under Rs 25,000 for most Indian homes -- 7-litre tank, mineralizer stage that adds back calcium and magnesium, and the widest service network in India. Runners-up are the Pureit Ultima for smaller families and the Kent Grand Plus for tech-forward users who want app connectivity.
key_takeaways: Mineralizer stage matters: pure RO water strips beneficial minerals and tastes flat -- spend the money on a purifier that adds them back.
Skip the Livpure Glo Pro: Rs 18,000 for a 5-litre tank with no mineralizer and slow refill rate -- the Aquaguard Aura is the same price with a 7L tank and TDS controller.
Service network beats specs on paper: Aquaguard has 600+ service centres across India, Kent has 250+, Pureit has 200+. Filter replacement turnaround time matters more than initial price.
7-litre tank is the sweet spot for a family of 4: smaller tanks need frequent refills, larger tanks waste energy keeping water cool.
who_for: Indian families in metros and tier-2 cities who use municipal tap water with TDS between 200-1500 ppm, want RO+UV protection, and need a service-backed purifier that survives 5+ years of use.
methodology: We compared 5 RO+UV water purifiers under Rs 25,000 available on Amazon India and Flipkart in September 2026. For each, we evaluated TDS handling (with and without mineralizer), tank size, filter life, service network coverage, and 90-day user review patterns. Picks were cross-checked against Eureka Forbes, HUL Pureit, and Kent annual maintenance contracts to surface total ownership cost.
